01.actor: Rava and the wealthy Rav Natan bar Ami
01.event: Rava forced Rav Natan bar Ami to give charity against his will.
01.turn: A wealthy man was compelled to give though he had no particular obligation.
01.outcome: Rava collected four hundred dinars from him for charity.
01.summary: Rava once coerced the wealthy Rav Natan bar Ami to donate to charity, and collected four hundred dinars from him. The incident is cited only as a precedent for forcing wealthy fathers to support their children, and it has no setup or reaction.
01.missing: Why Rava acted, Rav Natan's reaction, and any background to the incident.

02.actor: Rami bar Hama's sister and her husband Rav Avya
02.event: Her marriage contract was lost and the couple went to Rav Yosef to ask what to do.
02.turn: Rav Yosef answered with a ruling of Rabbi Meir that would make their marriage forbidden, and Abaye challenged it.
02.outcome: Rav Yosef conceded and told Rav Avya to go and write her a new marriage contract.
02.summary: Rami bar Hama's sister was married to Rav Avya, and her marriage contract was lost. They asked Rav Yosef, who answered by citing Rabbi Meir's strict view and the Sages' lenient one. Abaye objected that the law follows Rabbi Meir's decrees, and Rav Yosef told the husband to go write her a new contract.

03.actor: The members of the house of the prince and the judges Rabbi Abbahu and colleagues
03.event: The prince's household seized a maidservant of orphans for a debt, and the judges approved.
03.turn: Rabbi Abba accused the judges of flattering the powerful and noted that Reish Lakish had reversed a similar seizure.
03.outcome: Rabbi Abba's rebuke leaves the approval in doubt, and the text shows no formal result.
03.summary: The household of the prince seized an orphans' maidservant in an alley as payment for a debt. Rabbi Abbahu and the other judges said the seizure was good. Rabbi Abba asked whether they were flattering the prince's family, since Reish Lakish had overturned a similar act by judges who followed Rabbi Tarfon.
03.missing: What the judges decided after Rabbi Abba's objection.

04.actor: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei
04.event: He saw priestly gifts given directly to a priest's slave in Rabbi Yosei's locale, then testified about it in Rabbi Yehuda's locale.
04.turn: The court sought to elevate the slave to priesthood on his testimony, since in that locale eating teruma was taken as proof of priestly status.
04.outcome: The attempt to elevate the slave did not go through.
04.summary: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei, said he testified only once in his life. He had seen a priest's slave receive teruma in his father's locale, where that proves nothing, and then testified to it in Rabbi Yehuda's locale, where it does. The court wanted to elevate the slave to priesthood on this basis, but in the end it did not.

05.event: He served drinks at his son Abba Mar's wedding and poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak, son of Rav Yehuda.
05.turn: Rav Yitzhak did not stand up before him.
05.summary: Rav Pappa was serving drinks to guests at the wedding of his son Abba Mar. He poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak, son of Rav Yehuda, who did not stand before him. Rav Pappa became angry.

06.event: He went up to Eretz Yisrael and was ordained and seated on the calendar council.
06.turn: At each step he declared himself spared one more of the three curses in Ezekiel's verse.
06.summary: When Rabbi Elazar went up to Eretz Yisrael he said he had been spared one curse. When he was ordained he said two, and when he joined the calendar council he said three. The three curses come from Ezekiel's verse about false prophets, and he escaped each.

09.actor: A man who betrothed a woman with a myrtle mat
09.event: He betrothed a woman with a myrtle mat, and bystanders pointed out it was worth less than a peruta.
09.turn: He said she could be betrothed with the four dinars hidden in the mat, and she took it and was silent.
09.outcome: Rava ruled that her silence after the money was given counts for nothing.
09.summary: A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle mat. People told him it was worth less than a peruta, so he said she was betrothed with the four dinars inside it. She took the mat and said nothing, and Rava ruled that silence after receiving the money proves nothing.

10.event: Rav Beivai told the Sages not to trust Rav Yosef's report of a teaching.
10.turn: He said the teaching came from him in the name of Rav Adda bar Ahava, not from Rabbi, and Rav Yosef realized his mistake.
10.outcome: Rav Yosef exclaimed that he had confused the word Rabbi with the word rabbim.
10.summary: Rav Yosef reported a ruling in the name of Rabbi. Rav Beivai told the Sages not to listen, saying he had given it to Rav Yosef himself in the name of Rav Adda bar Ahava, and the word was rabbim (many). Rav Yosef exclaimed in astonishment that he had mistaken one word for the other.

11.event: A noblewoman tried to seduce Rav Kahana, a seller of palm baskets.
11.turn: He said he would go adorn himself, climbed to the roof and threw himself off, and Elijah caught him.
11.outcome: Elijah gave him a basket of dinars, ending his need for the trade.
11.summary: A noblewoman tried to seduce Rav Kahana, who sold palm baskets. He said he would go adorn himself, went up on the roof and fell. Elijah the prophet caught him and complained he had come four hundred parasangs. Rav Kahana blamed his poverty, and Elijah gave him a basket of dinars.

12.event: A marriage contract was brought to Rabbi Abbahu, with the scribe's handwriting and one witness's signature recognized.
12.turn: Rabbi Abbahu thought to validate it, but Rabbi Yirmeya said the mishna requires the scribe to have signed.
12.summary: A marriage contract came before Rabbi Abbahu. People recognized the scribe's handwriting and one witness's signature, and he was inclined to validate it. Rabbi Yirmeya objected that the mishna requires the scribe to have signed.
12.missing: Whether Rabbi Abbahu accepted the correction and what happened to the contract.

13.event: He was asked about the rival wife of a daughter and about whose view is the law.
13.turn: He refused to take sides between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel, fearing for his skull.
13.outcome: He instead testified that two great families, including High Priests, descended from rival wives.
13.summary: Rabbi Yehoshua was asked about the rival wife of a daughter and whose view is the law. He said it was a dispute of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel and asked why they were putting his head between two great mountains. He then testified that two great Jerusalem families, from which High Priests came, descended from rival wives.

15.actor: Rav Aha bar Abba and Rav Hisda
15.event: Rav Aha visited his son-in-law Rav Hisda and sat his granddaughter on his lap.
15.turn: Rav Hisda asked whether she might be betrothed, and each accused the other of violating a ruling of Rav or Shmuel.
15.outcome: Rav Aha began to cite a justifying statement of Shmuel, which is completed in the next segment.
15.summary: Rav Aha bar Abba visited his son-in-law Rav Hisda and put his granddaughter on his lap. Rav Hisda asked if she might be betrothed, and Rav Aha replied that Rav Hisda had broken Rav's rule on betrothing minors. Rav Hisda answered that Rav Aha had broken Shmuel's rule against using a woman, and Rav Aha cited another saying of Shmuel, that all is for the sake of Heaven.
15.missing: The passage is cut off mid-sentence; the end of Shmuel's quote is in the next segment, and no clear resolution is given.

16.event: Homa asked Rava for sustenance and wine, and while showing him the size of Abaye's cups her arm was uncovered.
16.turn: Her beauty lit up the courtroom and Rava went home and asked his wife for intimacy.
16.outcome: Rava's wife learned the cause and beat Homa with a chest lock until she was driven out of Mehoza.
16.summary: Abaye's widow Homa asked Rava to set her sustenance and also wine. To show how large Abaye's cups were, she bared her arm, and her beauty lit up the courtroom. Rava went home and asked his wife for intimacy. His wife asked who had been in court, learned it was Homa, chased her out of Mehoza with a chest lock, and accused her of having already killed three husbands.
